contingencyRemaining.rule: Contingency is not a slush fund for new tools or vendors. It is reserved for launch-critical incident response, validation blockers, and 72-hour stabilization. Any draw is Class C if already contemplated as contingency in the approved plan and logged; Class D if it is new, unbudgeted, or material beyond that reservation. Founder approval is required before treating a new vendor purchase as a contingency draw.

It does not record a contingency dollar split (for example, no $X operating / $Y contingency table is in the snapshot). Inventing a split would violate spendingAuthority.doNotInventOtherDollarThresholds.

freeze.title: No unplanned tool/vendor spend without visibility
rules: Every cash outflow during the launch period must have a daily-log entry before or immediately after the charge (same calendar day).

New vendors, paid ads/boosts, extra AI credit packs, new SaaS seats, and unbudgeted tools are Class D — blocked until Founder approval is recorded in aos_founder_decisions or an equivalent Founder-attested decision record.
Already-approved vendor auto-renewals (Class B) may continue so launch does not go dark; Michelle logs the amount when Founder or the vendor invoice makes it visible.
Workbook cost ranges are not a shopping list. Incomplete rows with $250–$750 testing/audit ranges do not authorize hiring vendors from this control.
If remaining cap is uncertified, treat capacity as scarce: do not initiate new Class C spend until Founder attests actuals or explicitly authorizes the specific Class C item.
Stripe, DNS, custom domain, and nameservers remain out of scope for agent mutation regardless of spend class.
